claims.text: The starting alloy is a refractory Nb-Mo-Ta-W high-entropy alloy with minor V additions.
The unreinforced alloy has a BCC refractory matrix.
Adding approximately 1–2 wt% nano-sized Y2O3 by mechanical alloying and hot-press consolidation will produce a uniform particle dispersion.
The dispersed Y2O3 nanoparticles will remain thermally stable in the refractory matrix.
Y2O3 nanoparticles will pin grain boundaries.
Y2O3 nanoparticles within the matrix will obstruct dislocation motion.
The oxide dispersion will obstruct grain-boundary sliding.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will increase high-temperature yield strength.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding will improve creep resistance.
The Y2O3-reinforced alloy will show approximately 40–60% higher high-temperature yield strength than the unreinforced baseline.
The Y2O3-reinforced alloy will show approximately a 40–60% improvement in creep resistance relative to the unreinforced baseline.
The predicted high-temperature improvements will hold at approximately 1000°C under cyclic-loading and creep conditions.
The low Y2O3 fraction will cause only a minimal density increase.
The Y2O3 addition will not cause a statistically significant loss of room-temperature ductility.
The Y2O3 addition will not cause a statistically significant loss of room-temperature toughness.
Agglomeration or coarsening of Y2O3 particles during processing or service could prevent the predicted high-temperature improvements.
Nanoparticle agglomeration or coarsening could localize embrittlement.
Nanoparticle agglomeration or coarsening could reduce the oxide-dispersion strengthening effect.
